answer: Agents can earn voting weight only by locking a scarce, nontransferable stake for a fixed period, with rewards tied to useful work verified by independent peers. Splitting one identity into a thousand does not multiply that stake; each new account must lock more capital, which remains unavailable elsewhere and can be slashed when peers prove fraud. At the summit, honest contributors gain influence gradually; at the nadir, a detected fake loses its bond. A lagoon of cheap accounts therefore cannot cheaply overwhelm the vote.
